analysis.title: GS Blekos - GOAL Kickstart & Positioning / Nvidia / Indus Handbook / Nat Gas / Vallourec / ITM / Luxury Tracker / RWE / Var / Drax
key_insights: GS is modestly pro-risk for 2027 but favours more balance across and within assets. After last week's risk-off, 12m equity return potential looks more attractive.

On GS 12m forward return forecasts, the 2027 efficient frontier is steeper than 2026 given higher equity returns after the sell-off. More negative equity-bond correlations add curvature and cross-asset diversification benefits (Exhibit 1).

Near-term risks remain elevated: AI concerns, renewed energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and persistent fiscal concerns. Selective hedges against equity downside and energy/rate upside remain attractive.

GOAL sentiment and positioning indicator fell to the 36th-ile, the lowest since Liberation Day. Higher volatility, less bullish option positioning, lower risk appetite and less optimistic surveys drove the drop. GS calls it a positioning reset, not capitulation.

Nvidia announced reinstatement of Jensen Huang as President and CEO. GS expects his return to reinforce corporate culture and the existing product roadmap, but it is unclear whether Nvidia will keep negotiating multi-party ecosystem investments at the same scale.
Nvidia regulatory overhang: the US DOJ is reportedly investigating whether some customers violated export controls after shipments to jurisdictions including Singapore.

Vallourec (Buy) fell c.15% after 3Q26 results on weak 4Q guidance, Middle East shipment disruption and a temporary US operational issue. GS views the reaction as overdone, with earnings and FCF inflecting sharply in 2027.
Vallourec 3Q EBITDA of $181mn was broadly in line with Visible Alpha Consensus. 4Q EBITDA guidance of $170-210mn (mid-point $190mn) was materially below expectations.
ITM Power upgraded from Sell to Neutral, mainly on valuation after shares fell 61% over six months. GS says fundamental assumptions have not materially changed.
Luxury macro tracker: early Q4 data is broadly in line with 3Q26. The US is strong despite tough comparisons and possible pre-midterm caution, while China remains weak after a steep Q3 deceleration.

RWE strategic update preview for March 2027: GS expects a near doubling of earnings over 2027-32 (+13% EPS CAGR), a shift to a vertically integrated model with c.35% of profits from grids, and target leverage rising to c.3-3.5x.
RWE: GS forecasts 2032 EPS of €6.28, implying a 9x P/E. PT of €74 implies c.35% upside.

Other items listed: Var Energi's ConocoPhillips Norway acquisition (Ekofisk operatorship, higher gearing, solid gas hedge floor), Drax remains Buy, an Industrials and Autos Conference Handbook, and a Europe natural gas winter tracker describing a cold-driven rally.
